It’s something that birds sit on.

steps.prompt: What does the word that do here?
options: It joins the sentence to a second part which describes the thing.
It asks a question about the thing the sentence names.
It makes the sentence negative instead of positive.
steps.answer: It joins the sentence to a second part which describes the thing.
steps.why: A defining relative clause tells you which thing or person we mean. Without it the sentence is incomplete.

steps.title: who / which / that / where
steps.html:
Use it forExample
who — a personThe neighbour who fixes electronics.
which — a thingThe dish which has not worked since 2019.
that — a person or a thingThe chest of drawers that her father made.
where — a placeThe room where the guests sleep.

The relative word comes straight after the noun it describes: the thing which hangs above the basin.

That can replace who and which in this kind of clause. It cannot replace where.

Do not repeat the noun with a pronoun: say the man who lives here, not the man who he lives here.

This is how you name a thing when the word has gone: It’s the thing that you clean the floor with.

You will use exactly this pattern again in Unit 5, Lesson 15, to explain a word you don’t know.

steps.title: Before you read: the writer is looking after a stranger’s house for a month.
steps.sub: What do you think will be hardest about it?

steps.title: The house where I’m staying
steps.html:
I’m house-sitting for a friend of a friend this month. I’ve never met the owners — they’re the people who put an advert on a house-swap website, and I answered it.

The house is beautiful and completely strange to me. In the kitchen there’s a machine which washes the dishes, but I can’t find the button that starts it. There’s no proper cooker either, only the box that heats food in two minutes. I love cooking, so that is the thing which disappoints me most.

The bathroom is the room where everything confuses me. The bowl you wash your hands in looks like a sheet of paper, and on the first morning I couldn’t work the metal thing the water comes out of. There are candles everywhere, and towels so soft that I am almost afraid to use them.

In the bedroom there is nowhere to put my clothes — no tall cupboard where you hang things, and no low one with drawers either. There are white rugs on every floor, which is a problem for someone who spills things.

Outside, on the wall, there’s a big round dish that points at the sky, and a small camera which watches the front door. My friend says the owners collect old maps, and that the frames in the hall are worth more than my car. I am being very careful.

I’m enjoying it. But I still miss my own bed, my own duvet, and a kitchen where I know what everything is called.

Source note. Written for this course. The situation and the objects come from the house-sitting accounts in the Navigate B1 Unit 2 recordings.

In the bedroom there is nowhere to put my clothes — no tall cupboard where you hang things, and no low one with drawers either. There are white rugs on every floor, which is a problem for someone who spills things.

Outside, on the wall, there’s a big round dish that points at the sky, and a small camera which watches the front door. My friend says the owners collect old maps, and that the frames in the hall are worth more than my car. I am being very careful.

I’m enjoying it. But I still miss my own bed, my own duvet, and a kitchen where I know what everything is called.

steps.sub: Use these when the word has gone out of your head.

items.text: It’s the thing that you … with.

steps.title: Define five things in your home without naming them.
steps.sub: Write one sentence for each. Use who, which, that or where in every sentence.
steps.html:
1. Plan: one thing in the kitchen → one in the bathroom → one in the bedroom → one person → one room.
  • 1 It’s the thing that …
  • 2 It’s something which …
  • 3 It’s the room where …
  • 4 It’s a person who …
  • 5 It’s the place where …
